=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:209 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `reviewer_shared_pr_state` opens a new file descriptor on each call and never closes it.
  WHY: The watchdog repeatedly calls this function, so leaked descriptors accumulate until the process limit may be reached, causing lock acquisition to fail and degrading to uncoordinated lookups.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:207-213 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: When `flock -w 2` times out, waiting watchdogs perform uncoordinated PR-state lookups instead of consulting the shared cache before falling back.
  WHY: A lookup taking longer than two seconds can cause multiple reviewers to issue duplicate API requests, defeating the requirement that at most one worker perform the lookup per interval.
- tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py:~5037-5043, ~5060, ~5099 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The new tests use an immediate mocked `gh` response and do not exercise waiters timing out while the lock holder is still performing its API call.
  WHY: The contention failure can remain undetected because the tests cover immediate cache and lock paths but not the slow-leader scenario.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:207-213 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When `flock -w 2` times out, the fallback does not consult the shared cache before performing an uncoordinated lookup.
  WHY: A slow `gh_retry` call can make every waiting reviewer issue an independent API request, defeating deduplication.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:207-213 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The cache and lock-failure tests do not exercise waiters timing out while the lock holder is mid-API call.
  WHY: The mocked `gh` response is synchronous, leaving the slow-leader contention regression undetected.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:209 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `exec {shared_pr_lock_fd}>file` opens a new file descriptor on each invocation and never closes it.
  WHY: Long-running reviewer attempts accumulate descriptors until the limit may be reached, causing uncoordinated fallback lookups.
- Requirement: "Share a run-scoped, atomically updated PR-state observation with bounded freshness so at most one worker performs the existing lookup per interval." (Issue #6075, paragraph 1.)
  Expected change site: The `flock -w 2` lock-failure fallback at `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:207-213` — the fallback must consult the shared cache file (now in `${shared_pr_cache_path}`) before issuing its own API call, so that on lock-contention-with-slow-leader waiters still observe the leader's freshly-published result and only fall back to per-worker lookups when the cache is missing or stale past the freshness window.
  Evidence of absence: Lines 207-213 read `reviewer_pr_state_lookup || printf 'open\n'` directly, with no `cat "${shared_pr_cache_path}"` step in between. The cache read exists only inside the lock-held branch (lines 220-230), so a worker that times out on the flock never gets a chance to read whatever the lock holder has just published.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: CLAUDE.md §20 — exactly one changelog fragment for any PR that changes behavior an operator or consumer repo would notice; consumer-repo receive every change shipped to `scripts/` on the next @stable sync, and `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh` changes reviewer runtime behavior.
  Expected change site: `changelog.d/6075-<slug>.md`
  Evidence of absence: The PR changed-files list contains only `.ai/.workspace_source_manifest.txt`, `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh`, and `tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py`; no `changelog.d/6075-*.md` file exists in the diff or in the repository. The PR description also does not mention a deferral.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
